description: Graph-native `session -has_affordance-> affordance` mirror for worlds/browser.py's BrowserWorld, driven by the agent-authored `ReachableFrom(node, edge_type)` DSL Term (transitive closure over one edge type) instead of Python-side flattening. The DOM `contains` tree nests affordances at arbitrary depth (a <nav> wraps links, a <form> wraps inputs) and `element -affords-> affordance` only ever fires on the affording element itself; before `ReachableFrom` existed there was no Term that could walk the unbounded-depth `contains` chain from a rule, so worlds/browser.py maintained a flat `sess -has_affordance-> aff` mirror by hand in Python. `ReachableFrom` closes that gap: these two rules mint the mirror edge for exactly the reachable+present affording elements' affordances, and drop it once an element is no longer present -- so the flattening is graph data, not a host loop.

microtheory.name: browser_affordance_reach
microtheory.description: Rules that keep `session -has_affordance-> affordance` in sync with the DOM `contains*` tree via ReachableFrom, for any BrowserWorld session.
